sentences.text: Anteophthalmosuchus was an extinct goniopholidid neosuchian that reached lengths of 3.5 to 4 meters, with a skull measuring roughly 60 centimeters.
This animal is recognized by the absence of a lower jaw opening, very broad upper temporal openings, and a tiny eye cover bone that does not cross the eye socket.
Its massive size made it one of the largest crocodylomorphs of its time.
The original specimen, a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton from the Wealden Group on the Isle of Wight, was formally named Anteophthalmosuchus hooleyi in 2011.
Additional fossils from Belgium and the Escucha Formation in Spain were later assigned to this genus.
Scientists have documented ten separate fossil occurrences of this creature.
The small eye cover bone suggests the animal had limited vision compared to modern crocodilians.
This reptile belongs to the family Goniopholididae and is the type species for the genus Anteophthalmosuchus.
Genetic studies indicate it is most closely related to a species now known as Hulkepholis willetti.
It inhabited southern England, eastern Spain, and western Belgium between 132.6 and 110.1 million years ago.
